claims.text: Standard L-PBF CoCrFeNiMn components exhibit dimensional imprecision, internal porosity, microcracks, and high residual stresses.
Rapid solidification causes the stated defects and residual stresses in L-PBF CoCrFeNiMn components.
An effective secondary remelting pass can use approximately 30–50% of the primary laser energy and a scanning speed 50% slower than the primary pass.
Applying the secondary laser remelting pass after each layer will refine the CoCrFeNiMn microstructure.
Applying the secondary laser remelting pass after each layer will reduce residual stress.
The modified process will improve dimensional precision relative to conventional L-PBF.
The modified process will enhance mechanical integrity relative to conventional L-PBF.
The secondary laser pass reheats and partially remelts the freshly deposited layer.
Reheating and partial remelting promote localized annealing and controlled resolidification.
The secondary remelting process repairs internal porosity.
The secondary remelting process repairs microcracks.
The secondary remelting process homogenizes thermal gradients across the layer.
Real-time thermal monitoring can keep energy input within a window that prevents overheating and excessive grain growth.
Controlled energy input stabilizes melt-pool dynamics and microstructural evolution.
The modified process will improve dimensional precision by approximately 30% relative to conventional L-PBF.
The modified process will reduce internal pore volume by around 40% relative to conventional L-PBF.
The modified process will enhance tensile strength and impact resistance by approximately 25% relative to conventional L-PBF.
The intervention is expected to be effective under argon, with a substrate preheated to approximately 300°C and calibrated laser parameters.
Inadequate thermal monitoring or simulation calibration may cause overheating or unforeseen thermal gradients.
Similar remelting interventions have improved microstructural quality in other additive-manufacturing contexts.
